mostWorthwhile.text: Forming the planet-forming disk was satisfying because it brought the inherited rocky and icy dust into the young solar system.

leastWorthwhile.text: The first two actions felt somewhat predictable because each was the only offered combination, although they established the collapse and rotation.

surprise.text: I was surprised that planet formation begins before the Sun reaches sustained main-sequence hydrogen burning.

arbitrary.text: Combining the protostar with neutral hydrogen to produce the contracting young Sun felt somewhat indirect; I expected progress toward fusion, but the result explained continued accretion and contraction instead.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the inherited dust and ice become worlds and eventually a sea, especially given the useful explanations of the physical processes so far.
